subject: VAL
label: Grade 11 Commerce
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 11 Commerce Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 2 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Values, ethics and wellbeing
modules.outcome: apply an ethical framework to a case
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Values, ethics and wellbeing', you learn to apply an ethical framework to a case. You work with exam-style questions and written reasoning. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Values, ethics and wellbeing' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: apply an ethical framework to a case. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: Calm routine: name the feeling, breathe in for 4 counts and out for 6, talk to someone, do one small helpful thing. Plan screen time: 1 hour, then a 10-minute break. Method: Model run for 'Values, ethics and wellbeing'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Apply an ethical framework to a case: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Learn three lenses. Consequences asks which choice gives the best result for the people affected. Duties asks which rules or promises must be kept. Character asks what an honest, fair, caring person would do. Use all three on a case before you decide.

Step 2, Read a commerce case. A firm has made 50,000 units of a product and finds a defect that harms 1 in 2,000 users. Expected harm is 50,000 divided by 2,000, which is 25 people. A recall would cost the firm a large sum, and it could lose profit and customers.

Step 3, Apply consequences. Recall: avoids about 25 injuries and protects the firm's reputation over time, though it costs money now. Say nothing: saves cost now but risks injury, legal penalties and lost trust later. Compare short-term and long-term effects.

Step 4, Apply duties and character. The firm has a duty to sell safe goods, to be honest with customers and to follow product-safety law. A fair, honest business leader would warn users and fix the problem, even at a price.

Step 5, Decide and justify. Write: 'The firm should recall, because the consequences, duties and character lenses agree.' Then name a cost and how to reduce it, such as refunds and clear notices. Wellbeing also matters; people who act ethically often sleep better.

Step 6, Your turn: a seller knows a battery overheats in 1 of 500 units out of 10,000 sold. Find the expected number of faulty units and say what to do. Answer: 10,000 divided by 500 is 20 units; warn buyers and recall them.

modules.title: Career and higher-study pathways
modules.outcome: map interests to courses and careers
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Career and higher-study pathways', you learn to map interests to courses and careers. You work with exam-style questions and written reasoning. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Career and higher-study pathways' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: map interests to courses and careers. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: List 3 strengths, 3 interests and 3 job families; match one to a course and write a next step with a date. Method: Model run for 'Career and higher-study pathways'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Map interests to courses and careers: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Self-assessment: Sana rates her interests from 1 to 5 using real activity evidence: Numbers 5 (she wins the maths quiz), Business ideas 4 (she runs a class stall), People 3, Writing 2. She does not pick a career yet.

Step 2, Course profiles: She gives weights for numbers, business, people and writing. Accounting and finance 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1. Marketing 0.1, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2. Human resources 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.2. Each row adds to 1.
Step 3, Score Accounting and finance: 5 times 0.5 is 2.5; 4 times 0.3 is 1.2; 3 times 0.1 is 0.3; 2 times 0.1 is 0.2. Total 2.5 plus 1.2 plus 0.3 plus 0.2 is 4.2 out of 5.

Step 4, Score the others: Marketing is 0.5 plus 1.6 plus 0.9 plus 0.4, which is 3.4. Human resources is 0.5 plus 0.8 plus 1.5 plus 0.4, which is 3.2. Ranking: Accounting and finance 4.2, Marketing 3.4, Human resources 3.2.

Step 5, Test the match: Sana checks entry needs: strong maths and accounting marks, and admission requirements on university pages. She asks a local accountant about a typical day and spends a day shadowing at a small firm to see if the work suits her.

Step 6, Plan with options: Her pathway is a bachelor course in accounting or finance, with professional exams later, and a second option in marketing. She writes what to do this term: raise her maths mark, join the finance club, and revisit her scores next year.

Your turn: Ratings Numbers 3, Business 5, People 4, Writing 3 with Marketing weights 0.1, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2. Model answer: 0.3 plus 2.0 plus 1.2 plus 0.6 is 4.1 out of 5, a strong match worth exploring through a short work experience.

ladder: L1: kindness, honesty and sharing in daily life.
L2: responsibility, courage and care for others and nature.
L3: fairness, respect for difference and service.
L5: leadership, wellbeing and ethical reasoning.
L6 (degree): applied ethics, culture and community work.
L7 (postgraduate): scholarship, counselling or teaching at depth.
